Charles I of Anjou.fact: Manfred staged a coup in Rome, but the Guelphs elected Charles senator (or the head of the civil government of Rome). He accepted the office, at which a group of cardinals requested that the Pope revoke the agreement with him, but the Pope, being otherwise defenceless against Manfred, could not break with Charles.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Foulquois also persuaded the _____ and Provençal prelates to offer financial support for the crusade
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Foulquois also persuaded the French and Provençal prelates to offer financial support for the crusade.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Foulquois was elected pope in February _____; he soon confirmed Charles's senatorship and urged him to come to Rome
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Foulquois was elected pope in February 1265; he soon confirmed Charles's senatorship and urged him to come to Rome.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles agreed that he would hold the _____ of Sicily as the popes' vassal for an annual tribute of 8,000 ounces of gold
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles agreed that he would hold the Kingdom of Sicily as the popes' vassal for an annual tribute of 8,000 ounces of gold.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He embarked at _____ on 10 May and landed at Ostia ten days later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He embarked at Marseilles on 10 May and landed at Ostia ten days later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He was installed as senator on 21 _____ and four cardinals invested him with the Regno a week later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He was installed as senator on 21 June and four cardinals invested him with the Regno a week later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: To finance further military actions he borrowed money from _____ bankers with the Pope's assistance, who had authorised him to pledge Church property
Charles I of Anjou.fact: To finance further military actions he borrowed money from Italian bankers with the Pope's assistance, who had authorised him to pledge Church property.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Five cardinals crowned him king of Sicily on 5 January _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Five cardinals crowned him king of Sicily on 5 January 1266. He left Rome on 20 January 1266.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He left Rome on 20 January _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Five cardinals crowned him king of Sicily on 5 January 1266. He left Rome on 20 January 1266.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The crusaders from _____ and Provence—reportedly 6,000 fully equipped mounted warriors, 600 mounted bowmen and 20,000 foot-soldiers—arrived in Rome ten days later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The crusaders from France and Provence—reportedly 6,000 fully equipped mounted warriors, 600 mounted bowmen and 20,000 foot-soldiers—arrived in Rome ten days later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles decided to invade southern _____ without delay, because he was unable to finance a lengthy campaign
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles decided to invade southern Italy without delay, because he was unable to finance a lengthy campaign.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He marched towards _____, but changed his strategy after learning of a muster of Manfred's forces near Capua
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He marched towards Naples, but changed his strategy after learning of a muster of Manfred's forces near Capua.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He led his troops across the _____ towards Benevento
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He led his troops across the Apennines towards Benevento.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Worried that further delays might endanger his subjects' loyalty, Manfred attacked Charles's army, then in disarray from the crossing of the hills, on 26 February _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Worried that further delays might endanger his subjects' loyalty, Manfred attacked Charles's army, then in disarray from the crossing of the hills, on 26 February 1266.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In the ensuing battle, _____'s army was defeated and he was killed
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Manfred also hurried to the town and reached it before Charles. Worried that further delays might endanger his subjects' loyalty, Manfred attacked Charles's army, then in disarray from the crossing of the hills, on 26 February 1266.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Resistance throughout the _____ collapsed and towns surrendered even before Charles's troops reached them
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Resistance throughout the Regno collapsed and towns surrendered even before Charles's troops reached them.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Saracens of _____—a Muslim colony established during Frederick II's reign—paid homage to him
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Saracens of Lucera—a Muslim colony set up during Frederick II's reign—paid homage to him.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His commander, Philip of _____, took control of the island of Sicily
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His commander, Philip of Montfort, took control of the island of Sicily.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles laid claim to her dowry—the island of Corfu and the region of _____ (now Durrës in Albania)—by right of conquest
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles laid claim to her dowry—the island of Corfu and the region of Durazzo (now Durrës in Albania)—by right of conquest.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His troops seized _____ before the end of the year
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles laid claim to her dowry—the island of Corfu and the region of Durazzo (now Durrës in Albania)—by right of conquest. His troops seized Corfu before the end of the year.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: They knew that he had promised to return estates to the _____ lords expelled from the Regno
Charles I of Anjou.fact: They knew that he had promised to return estates to the Guelph lords expelled from the Regno.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He also traded in grain, spices and sugar, through a joint venture with _____ merchants
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He also traded in grain, spices and sugar, through a joint venture with Pisan merchants.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The consolidation of Charles's power in northern Italy also alarmed _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement censured Charles for his methods of state administration, describing him as an arrogant and obstinate monarch. The consolidation of Charles's power in northern Italy also alarmed Clement.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: To appease the Pope, Charles resigned his senatorship in May _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: To appease the Pope, Charles resigned his senatorship in May 1267. Charles's troops ousted the Ghibellines from Florence in April 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's troops ousted the Ghibellines from Florence in April _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: To appease the Pope, Charles resigned his senatorship in May 1267. Charles's troops ousted the Ghibellines from Florence in April 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His successors, _____ and Luca Savelli, demanded the re-payment of the money that Charles and the Pope had borrowed from the Romans
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His successors, Conrad Monaldeschi and Luca Savelli, demanded the re-payment of the money that Charles and the Pope had borrowed from the Romans.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Victories by the _____, the imperial family's supporters, forced the Pope to ask Charles to send his troops to Tuscany
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Victories by the Ghibellines, the imperial family's supporters, forced the Pope to ask Charles to send his troops to Tuscany. Charles's troops ousted the Ghibellines from Florence in April 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After being elected the _____à (ruler) of Florence and Lucca for seven years, Charles hurried to Tuscany
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After being elected the Podestà (ruler) of Florence and Lucca for seven years, Charles hurried to Tuscany.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's expansionism along the _____' borders alarmed Pope Clement and he decided to change the direction of Charles's ambitions
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's expansionism along the Papal States' borders alarmed Pope Clement and he decided to change the direction of Charles's ambitions.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Pope summoned him to _____, forcing him to promise that he would abandon all claims to Tuscany in three years
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Pope summoned him to Viterbo, forcing him to promise that he would abandon all claims to Tuscany in three years.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He persuaded Charles to conclude agreements with _____ of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, and the titular Latin emperor Baldwin II in late May
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He persuaded Charles to conclude agreements with William of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, and the titular Latin emperor Baldwin II in late May.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: According to the first treaty, _____ acknowledged Charles's suzerainty and made Charles's younger son, Philip, his heir, also stipulating that Charles would inherit Achaea if Philip died childless
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He persuaded Charles to conclude agreements with William of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, and the titular Latin emperor Baldwin II in late May. According to the first treaty, Villehardouin acknowledged Charles's suzerainty and made Charles's younger son, Philip, his heir, also stipulating that Charles would inherit Achaea if Philip died childless.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles pledged that he would assist _____ in recapturing Constantinople from the Byzantine emperor, Michael VIII Palaiologos, in exchange for one third of the conquered lands
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles renounced Ventimiglia in favour of the Republic of Genoa to secure her neutrality. He defeated the rebels and forced Castellane into exile.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles returned to _____ and laid siege to the fortress of Poggibonsi, but it did not fall until the end of November
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles returned to Tuscany and laid siege to the fortress of Poggibonsi, but it did not fall until the end of November.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After Conradin accepted their proposal, _____'s former vicar in Sicily, Conrad Capece, returned to the island and stirred up a revolt
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Manfred's staunchest supporters had meanwhile fled to Bavaria to attempt to persuade Conrad IV's 15-year-old son Conradin to assert his hereditary right to the Kingdom of Sicily. After Conradin accepted their proposal, Manfred's former vicar in Sicily, Conrad Capece, returned to the island and stirred up a revolt.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Conradin left Bavaria in September _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Conradin left Bavaria in September 1267.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His supporters' revolt was spreading from Sicily to _____; the Saracens of Lucera also rose up
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His supporters' revolt was spreading from Sicily to Calabria; the Saracens of Lucera also rose up.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in Tuscany until March _____, when he met with the Pope
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in Tuscany until March 1268, when he met with the Pope. At the Battle of Tagliacozzo, on 23 August 1268, it appeared that Conradin had won the day, but a sudden charge by Charles's reserve routed Conradin's army.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: At the Battle of Tagliacozzo, on 23 August _____, it appeared that Conradin had won the day, but a sudden charge by Charles's reserve routed Conradin's army
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in Tuscany until March 1268, when he met with the Pope. At the Battle of Tagliacozzo, on 23 August 1268, it appeared that Conradin had won the day, but a sudden charge by Charles's reserve routed Conradin's army.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In April, the Pope made Charles imperial vicar of _____ "during the vacancy of the empire", a move of dubious legality
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Pope Clement urged Charles to return to the Regno, but he continued his campaign in Tuscany until March 1268, when he met with the Pope. In April, the Pope made Charles imperial vicar of Tuscany "during the vacancy of the empire", a move of dubious legality.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles marched to southern Italy and laid siege to _____, but he then had to hurry north to prevent Conradin's invasion of Abruzzo in late August
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His supporters' revolt was spreading from Sicily to Calabria; the Saracens of Lucera also rose up. Charles marched to southern Italy and laid siege to Lucera, but he then had to hurry north to prevent Conradin's invasion of Abruzzo in late August.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The burghers of _____, Aversa and other towns in Basilicata and Apulia massacred their fellows who had agitated on Conradin's behalf, but the Sicilians and the Saracens of Lucera did not surrender
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The burghers of Potenza, Aversa and other towns in Basilicata and Apulia massacred their fellows who had agitated on Conradin's behalf, but the Sicilians and the Saracens of Lucera did not surrender.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles marched to Rome where he was again elected senator in _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles marched to Rome where he was again elected senator in September.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: During the following decade, _____ was ruled by Charles's vicars, each appointed for one year
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles marched to Rome where he was again elected senator in September. During the following decade, Rome was ruled by Charles's vicars, each appointed for one year.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Conradin was captured at _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Conradin was captured at Torre Astura.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Most of his retainers were summarily executed, but _____ and his friend, Frederick I, Margrave of Baden, were brought to trial for robbery and treason in Naples
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Conradin was captured at Torre Astura. Most of his retainers were summarily executed, but Conradin and his friend, Frederick I, Margrave of Baden, were brought to trial for robbery and treason in Naples.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: They were sentenced to death and beheaded on 29 _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: They were sentenced to death and beheaded on 29 October.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Conrad of _____ was Conradin's only partisan to be released, but only after his wife threatened to execute the Guelph lords she held captive in her castle
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Conrad of Antioch was Conradin's only partisan to be released, but only after his wife threatened to execute the Guelph lords she held captive in her castle.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Ghibelline noblemen of the Regno fled to the court of _____ of Aragon, who had married Manfred's daughter Constance
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Ghibelline noblemen of the Regno fled to the court of Peter III of Aragon, who had married Manfred's daughter Constance.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The widowed Charles married Margaret of Nevers in November _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The widowed Charles married Margaret of Nevers in November 1268.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: She was co-heiress to her father, Odo, the eldest son of _____, Duke of Burgundy
Charles I of Anjou.fact: She was co-heiress to her father, Odo, the eldest son of Hugh IV, Duke of Burgundy.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The papal vacancy lasted for three years, which strengthened Charles's authority in _____, but it also deprived him of the ecclesiastic support that only a pope could provide
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The papal vacancy lasted for three years, which strengthened Charles's authority in Italy, but it also deprived him of the ecclesiastic support that only a pope could provide.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles returned to Lucera to personally direct its siege in April _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles returned to Lucera to personally direct its siege in April 1269. The Saracens and the Ghibellines who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Saracens and the Ghibellines who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles returned to Lucera to personally direct its siege in April 1269. The Saracens and the Ghibellines who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles made William l'Estandart the commander of the army in Sicily in August _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles returned to Lucera to personally direct its siege in April 1269. The Saracens and the Ghibellines who had escaped to the town resisted until starvation forced them to surrender in August 1269.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles sent _____ and Guy of Montfort to Sicily to force the rebels there into submission, but they could only capture Augusta
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles sent Philip and Guy of Montfort to Sicily to force the rebels there into submission, but they could only capture Augusta.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: L'_____ captured Agrigento, forcing Frederick of Castile and Frederick Lancia to seek refuge in Tunis
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles made William l'Estandart the commander of the army in Sicily in August 1269. L'Estandart captured Agrigento, forcing Frederick of Castile and Frederick Lancia to seek refuge in Tunis.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After L'Estandart's subsequent victory at Sciacca, only Capece resisted, but he also had to surrender in early _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After L'Estandart's subsequent victory at Sciacca, only Capece resisted, but he also had to surrender in early 1270. Charles's troops forced Siena and Pisa—the last towns to resist him in Tuscany—to sue for peace in August 1270.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's troops forced Siena and Pisa—the last towns to resist him in Tuscany—to sue for peace in August _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After L'Estandart's subsequent victory at Sciacca, only Capece resisted, but he also had to surrender in early 1270. Charles's troops forced Siena and Pisa—the last towns to resist him in Tuscany—to sue for peace in August 1270.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He granted privileges to the _____ merchants and bankers which strengthened their position in the Regno
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's troops forced Siena and Pisa—the last towns to resist him in Tuscany—to sue for peace in August 1270. He granted privileges to the Tuscan merchants and bankers which strengthened their position in the Regno.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: His influence was declining in _____, because the Lombard towns no longer feared an invasion from Germany after Conradin's death
Charles I of Anjou.fact: His influence was declining in Lombardy, because the Lombard towns no longer feared an invasion from Germany after Conradin's death.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In May _____ Charles sent Walter of La Roche to represent him in the province, but this failed to strengthen his authority
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In May 1269 Charles sent Walter of La Roche to represent him in the province, but this failed to strengthen his authority.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The Lombard towns accepted the invitation, but some towns—Milan, _____, Alessandria and Tortona—only confirmed their alliance with Charles, without acknowledging his rule
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The Lombard towns accepted the invitation, but some towns—Milan, Bologna, Alessandria and Tortona—only confirmed their alliance with Charles, without acknowledging his rule.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: According to his confessor, _____ of Beaulieu, Louis was convinced that al-Mustansir of Tunis was ready to convert to Christianity
Charles I of Anjou.fact: According to his confessor, Geoffrey of Beaulieu, Louis was convinced that al-Mustansir of Tunis was ready to convert to Christianity.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The French crusaders embarked at Aigues-Mortes on 2 July _____; Charles departed from Naples six days later
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The French crusaders embarked at Aigues-Mortes on 2 July 1270; Charles departed from Naples six days later.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He spent more than a month in _____, waiting for his fleet
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He spent more than a month in Sicily, waiting for his fleet.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: By the time he landed at Tunis on 25 _____, dysentery and typhoid fever had decimated the French army
Charles I of Anjou.fact: By the time he landed at Tunis on 25 August, dysentery and typhoid fever had decimated the French army.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The crusaders twice defeated Al-_____'s army, forcing him to sue for peace
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The crusaders twice defeated Al-Mustansir's army, forcing him to sue for peace. According to the peace treaty, signed on 1 November, Al-Mustansir agreed to fully compensate Louis' son and successor, Philip III of France, and Charles for the expenses of the military campaign and to release his Christian prisoners.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He also promised to pay a yearly tribute to Charles and to expel Charles's opponents from _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He also promised to pay a yearly tribute to Charles and to expel Charles's opponents from Tunis. The gold from Tunis, along with silver from the newly opened mine at Longobucco, enabled Charles to mint new coins, called carlini, in the Regno.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The gold from Tunis, along with silver from the newly opened mine at _____, enabled Charles to mint new coins, known as carlini, in the Regno
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The gold from Tunis, along with silver from the newly opened mine at Longobucco, enabled Charles to mint new coins, called carlini, in the Regno.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles and _____ departed Tunis on 10 November
Charles I of Anjou.fact: According to the peace treaty, signed on 1 November, Al-Mustansir agreed to fully compensate Louis' son and successor, Philip III of France, and Charles for the expenses of the military campaign and to release his Christian prisoners. Charles and Philip departed Tunis on 10 November.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: A storm dispersed their fleet at _____ and most of Charles's galleys were lost or damaged
Charles I of Anjou.fact: A storm dispersed their fleet at Trapani and most of Charles's galleys were lost or damaged.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.fact: Genoese ships returning from the crusade were also sunk or forced to land in Sicily. Before leaving Sicily he granted temporary tax concessions to the Sicilians, because he realised that the conquest of the island had caused much destruction.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Charles I of Anjou.fact: Genoese ships returning from the crusade were also sunk or forced to land in Sicily. Before leaving Sicily he granted temporary tax concessions to the Sicilians, because he realised that the conquest of the island had caused much destruction.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles seized the damaged ships and their cargo, ignoring all protests from the _____ authorities of Genoa
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles seized the damaged ships and their cargo, ignoring all protests from the Ghibelline authorities of Genoa.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's brother, _____ of Poitiers, fell ill
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's brother, Alphonse of Poitiers, fell ill. Charles sent his best doctors to cure him, but Alphonse died.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles sent his best doctors to cure him, but _____ died
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's brother, Alphonse of Poitiers, fell ill. Charles sent his best doctors to cure him, but Alphonse died.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: He claimed the major part of _____'s inheritance, including the Marquisate of Provence and the County of Poitiers, because he was Alphonse's nearest kin
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's brother, Alphonse of Poitiers, fell ill. Charles sent his best doctors to cure him, but Alphonse died.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: After Philip III objected, he took the case to the _____ of Paris
Charles I of Anjou.fact: After Philip III objected, he took the case to the Parlement of Paris.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In _____ the court ruled that appanages escheated to the French crown if their rulers died without descendants
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In 1284 the court ruled that appanages escheated to the French crown if their rulers died without descendants.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: An earthquake destroyed the walls of _____ in the late 1260s or early 1270s
Charles I of Anjou.fact: An earthquake destroyed the walls of Durazzo in the late 1260s or early 1270s.

Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles's troops took possession of the town with the assistance of the leaders of the nearby _____ communities
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles's troops took possession of the town with the assistance of the leaders of the nearby Albanian communities. Charles concluded an agreement with the Albanian chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles concluded an agreement with the Albanian chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles concluded an agreement with the Albanian chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February 1272. Charles hurried to Rome to attend the enthronement of Pope Gregory X on 27 March 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.question: Charles hurried to Rome to attend the enthronement of Pope Gregory X on 27 March _____
Charles I of Anjou.fact: Charles concluded an agreement with the Albanian chiefs, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties in February 1272. Charles hurried to Rome to attend the enthronement of Pope Gregory X on 27 March 1272.

Charles I of Anjou.question: He adopted the title of King of Albania and appointed _____ as his vicar-general
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He adopted the title of King of Albania and appointed Gazzo Chinardo as his vicar-general.

Charles I of Anjou.question: He also sent his fleet to _____ to defend the principality against Byzantine attacks
Charles I of Anjou.fact: He also sent his fleet to Achaea to defend the principality against Byzantine attacks.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: The new pope was determined to put an end to the conflicts between the _____ and the Ghibellines
Charles I of Anjou.fact: The new pope was determined to put an end to the conflicts between the Guelphs and the Ghibellines. In November 1272 Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all Genoese within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: While in _____ met with the Guelph leaders who had been exiled from Genoa
Charles I of Anjou.fact: While in Rome Charles met with the Guelph leaders who had been exiled from Genoa.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports
Charles I of Anjou.question: In November _____ Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all Genoese within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property
Charles I of Anjou.fact: In November 1272 Charles commanded his officials to take prisoner all Genoese within his territories, except for the Guelphs, and to seize their property.

Charles I of Anjou.subject: Sports

Chess.fact: There is no universally accepted way to delineate the three phases of the game; the middlegame is typically considered to have begun after 10–20 moves, and the endgame when only a few pieces remain.  ==== Opening ==== Competitive players typically learn, memorize, and play well-documented sequences of opening moves.  The most common starting moves for White are 1. d4, which usually lead to substantially different types of positions, and Black has multiple viable responses to both.  Sequences of opening moves are referred to as openings and are catalogued in reference works, such as the Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings.  There are thousands of openings, though only a small fraction of them are commonly played; variations of openings may also be given names.  Openings vary widely in character from quiet positional play (for example, the Réti Opening) to sharp aggressive play (like the Latvian Gambit)

Chess.fact: The middlegame is the phase in which most combinations occur.  Combinations are a series of tactical moves executed to achieve some gain.  Middlegame combinations are often connected with an attack against the opponent's king.  Some typical patterns have their own names; for example, the Boden's Mate or the Lasker–Bauer combination.  Specific plans or strategic themes will often arise from particular groups of openings that result in a specific type of pawn structure.  An example is the minority attack, which is the attack of queenside pawns against an opponent who has more pawns on the queenside.  The study of openings is therefore connected to the preparation of plans that are typical of the resulting middlegames
